name: Qwen Concept 27B
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear attention with full gated attention every 4th layer (16 of 64); partial RoPE
notes: ADDED 2026-11-13 from the trending feed (trendingScore 132, created 2026-11-08, 175 likes). NOT a fine-tune: Qwen3.8-27B with nine down-projection matrices (layers 32-48 even) rewritten by a rank-one additive term derived from the model's own residual activations. No gradient step, no training data, no preference optimisation. derivative_kind is 'other' because the schema's enum has no weight-editing member - the closest honest label; it is not an abliteration and not a merge. PARAMS/ARCH: safetensors index and config.json are the base's own, so every architecture field above is inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (models/qwen3-8-27b): 64 layers, hybrid Gated DeltaNet with full gated attention every 4th layer (16 of 64), hidden 5120, 16 query / 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, 262144 native context. active_params_b equals params_b (dense, no MoE); flops_per_token_active = 2 x 27.781e9 = 5.556e10 on the schema's one-pass basis. KV: 65,536 B/token inherited - 16 full-attention layers x 2 x 4 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 2 B; the 48 linear-attention layers hold a constant state and are excluded. HARDWARE GATE: passes - 27.781B active (<= 40) and 27.781 x 0.5 = 13.9 GiB at the catalog's 4-bit planning figure (<= 128). Dense, so nothing is offloaded per token; the release ships bf16 (~52 GB), FP8_BLOCK (~30 GB), NVFP4 W4A16 (~20 GB), Q8_0 GGUF (~27 GB) and Q4_K_M GGUF (~16 GB). WHAT THE EVIDENCE IS: the paper (working paper v1, 2026-11-08, concept.country) is a controlled replication with a pre-registered success criterion and, crucially, a NORM-MATCHED RANDOM CONTROL - the same nine matrices perturbed to the same ||dW|| in a random orthogonal direction. The control moves nothing (GPQA -1.0 [-3.3,+1.3], IFBench -1.3 [-6.0,+3.3], LCB +3.0 [-3.8,+9.9]; no token saving anywhere), so the effect is directional rather than a small-perturbation artefact. That control is why this record exists at all. WHAT IT WINS: three benchmarks, all measured against a base the authors re-ran themselves on one GB10 with Q8_0 GGUF - GPQA Diamond 81.8 -> 86.1 (+4.3, CI excludes zero), LiveCodeBench v6 58.0 -> 71.0 (+13.0, CI excludes zero), and thinking tokens down 27-54% on every benchmark. WHAT IT LOSES / WHAT NOT TO CLAIM: (1) IFBench accuracy +3.3 has a CI that INCLUDES ZERO [-1.0,+7.7] and the authors explicitly decline to claim the IFBench control clause as borderline and bootstrap-seed dependent - it is recorded as printed, not as a win. (2) It does NOT beat the size class: the base's own published GPQA Diamond is 89.2 and LiveCodeBench v6 90.3 (models/qwen3-8-27b), both ABOVE this model's within-harness 86.1 and 71.0. The paper's baseline is 7.4pp (GPQA) and 32.3pp (LCB) under Qwen's card numbers, so the deltas are like-for-like inside one harness only and are NOT size-class upsets. (3) All arms are Q8_0; the edit was never evaluated at bf16, FP8 or NVFP4, so the card's own warning is that a 4-bit conversion may not preserve the effect. (4) n=3 benchmarks, one model family, one size, one alpha (0.1), one engine - the paper says so. CONTAMINATION NOTE FROM THE PAPER: the authors document that a follow-up sampling run appended rows into the same result files (GPQA 633/792/396 rows against 396 per arm), silently mixing 2-sample and 4-sample problems; every number here is from the recomputed, sample-filtered artifacts.

benchmarks.name: GPQA Diamond
benchmarks.config: Paper Table 1 (concept.country PDF, working paper v1, 2026-11-08), edit vs unmodified base, paired by problem: 86.1 vs 81.8, delta +4.3 [95% CI +1.8, +7.1], 198 problems x 2 samples, 10,000-replicate bootstrap, thinking tokens -30.0% [-35.5, -24.6]. BASE COLUMN FOUND: do not read this as a win over Qwen's published 89.2 for the same test - the authors re-ran the base themselves on one GB10 with Q8_0 GGUF at 81.8, 7.4pp under Qwen's card number, so the delta is like-for-like inside their harness only. Norm-matched random control moved -1.0 [-3.3, +1.3]: the direction did the work, not the perturbation magnitude.

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench v6
benchmarks.config: Same paper, Table 1: edit 71.0 vs base 58.0, delta +13.0 [+6.1, +20.6], 131 problems, thinking tokens -29.2%. Base's own published LCB v6 is 90.3 (catalog record models/qwen3-8-27b), so this is a within-harness delta, not a size-class upset. Control +3.0 [-3.8, +9.9] - not significant.

benchmarks.name: IFBench
benchmarks.config: Same paper, Table 1: edit 82.7 vs base 79.3, delta +3.3 [-1.0, +7.7] - the CI INCLUDES ZERO, recorded because the card prints it, not as a win. Token clause clears: -54.1% [-62.9, -45.6]. The authors explicitly decline to claim the IFBench control clause (borderline, seed-dependent). 300 problems.
